deliverables/colderwater-playground-devtools/final-cross-check-2026-09-27/harness/rewardkit-0.1.7-source/judges.py:313-318,460-600 and models.py:142 (harness reference for mode='individual'; read-only)
evidence: Scope: three scored dimensions (scoring.toml weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2); both gates use aggregation='all_pass' and are exempt. (1) polish: judge.toml mode='batched', aggregation='weighted_mean', 5 binary criteria. prompt.md:12 'A blank or static shell or an observed failure of that check gives binary0 throughout. Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.' prompt.md:24 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row.' prompt.md:22 makes a skipped step fail 'that criterion' only. (2) visual: mode='batched', weighted_mean, 5 likert criteria. prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' prompt.md:14 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row.' (3) functional: judge.toml:3 mode='individual' (template uses 'batched'), so each of the 15 criteria is graded in its own agent session; rewardkit 0.1.7 _arun_agent_individual (judges.py:467-494) loops criteria, calling _arun_agent_call with [c] alone, and a timeout zeros only that criterion (_timeout_scores). prompt.md:11 'This session grades exactly ONE criterion ... The other functional criteria are graded in separate sessions ... judge it against its own bar'; prompt.md:17 'continue after a failed leg so the report shows every leg'. Independence is therefore structural and also worded. No scored prompt, criterion description or app_context contains stop-at-first-failure wording (grep for stop/abort/remaining criteria/rest of/throughout/skip in scored judge.toml and app_context.md: only per-leg 'stop'-free hits; 'binary0 throughout' appears only for the global gate failure). The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the in-dimension global browser gate, which the template itself sanctions ('The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension'); it is a precondition identical in substance to the constraints gate criterion hro_gate_shared, so an app that fails it already gets reward 0 from the gate. Cross-row dependencies are handled per criterion, not by cascading zero: functional prompt.md:21 lets a leg whose setup is blocked by another criterion's feature be judged against the state produced or left out; polish judge.toml criteria say 'how quickly it arrived is graded only in Functional', 'that is graded in Functional'. Lessons file check: lesson 9 (report each step / skipped step fails) is present in all three prompts and scoped to 'that criterion'; lesson 16 (no double grading) is addressed by 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' and 'scored elsewhere' notes; lesson 11 (infra crash zeroes a dimension) is a harness behaviour outside this row's wording scope. Adversarial: (a) broken app that could pass - an app failing the first polish row cannot zero the other four because the prompt mandates continuing; no wording lets a single miss cascade. (b) conforming app that could fail - a correct app failing only by judge flake on the in-dimension gate would lose all of batched polish/visual, but that is the template-sanctioned gate, not a criterion miss, and in functional it affects only that one session. Run verdict: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'); this row is a prompt-wording check, so the wording is verified by reading, while actual judge compliance remains unmeasured.
